ColonyCouncil.AdvisorSignalDef.label: a bedroom fit for a title

tips.li: A noble whose bedroom falls short of their title feels it every day, and higher titles ask for more: more space, more impressiveness, a bedside table and a dresser.
Space is the one thing upgrading can't add; a room too small has to be built anew.
Impressiveness comes cheapest from a good floor, a piece of art and furniture of good quality.
One stove means one cook at a time, however many the colony has. A second lets two work side by side.
Cooking in bulk saves time once there's a stove to spare: set one bill to make four meals at once.
Keep the stoves close to the freezer, so the cooks don't spend the day walking for ingredients.
Below freezing, food doesn't rot at all. Whatever doesn't fit in the freezer starts its clock again.
Things that keep on their own (rice, corn, cloth, medicine) can move out of the freezer to make room for meat and meals.
[!lowtech] A bigger freezer needs more cooling: count on another cooler for each step up in size.
A double door, or an airlock of two doors, keeps the cold in while people go in and out.
Space counts the floor nobody's furniture stands on. Tables, chairs and statues all eat into it.
A cramped room weighs on everyone who spends time in it, and the dining room is where everyone spends time.
The planner keeps the turn, the style and the materials when you switch to a larger size of the same room.
Work goes slower in the dark, and a workshop works long after sunset.
A chair on a bench's work spot lets the crafter sit while they work, and keeps up their comfort through a long bill.
"Plan chairs and lamps" puts a chair on each empty work spot and hangs lamps where the benches are dark.
Prisoners mind eating off the floor and sitting in the dark like anyone else, and an unhappy prisoner is likelier to break or try to escape.
An impressive cell lifts a prisoner's mood. A floor, a light and a table go a long way.
Someone the colony hopes to recruit joins more willingly from a cell they can bear.
